images.caption:
Remnants of the Kinzua Viaduct, a railroad bridge spanning the gorge of Kinzua Creek, McKean County. It was the tallest and longest bridge of its kind when it was built in the early 1880s. Its history is discussed here.

A tornado collapsed a large section of the structurally weak bridge in 2003. The damage wasn't confined to the bridge; much of the surrounding forest was leveled. A revitalization project is set to begin; however, the bridge will not be rebuilt.

images.caption:
Standing portion of the Kinzua Viaduct, a railroad bridge spanning the gorge of Kinzua Creek, McKean County. 
A tornado collapsed a large section of the bridge in 2003. The standing portion of the bridge has been converted to a pedestrian walkway, with a glass-bottomed observation deck.

Photo of the bridge during my last visit, in 2007, here.

images.filename: Kinzua Bridge steelworks, Kinzua Bridge State Park, Pennsylvania - 20210317.jpg
images.caption: Looking across the valley of Kinzua Creek from below the deck of the Kinzua Bridge in March 2021. The steelwork seen here dates to the bridge's reconstruction in 1900, erected by the Elmira Bridge Company to a design by engineer C. R. Grimm. The structure cost $275.000 to build and contained 3,358 short tons of steel.
